The verb יוֹדוּ is a jussive plural; the five English versions split between 'Oh that men would' (KJV, ASV, Webster), 'Let men' (BBE) and an indicative (YLT). The subject of 'they became few' is not named; Ibn Ezra, Radak and Malbim read it as the same people who had just multiplied, and Rashi as the people at their start. 'Oṣer' (H6115) is glossed by STEPBible as 'pressure of', and the versions split: KJV 'oppression', YLT 'restraint', BBE folds it into 'trouble'. I chose 'restraint' for the literal layer and a gentler 'crushing weight' in the dramatic one.

Ibn Ezra, Radak and Meiri note that a conjunction is missing in the list, so 'oṣer rāʿāh weyagon' can be read as 'restraint, calamity and sorrow' (three items) or as 'the restraint of calamity and sorrow'. I kept the three-item reading, as KJV, YLT and ASV do.

agent_notes: KJV 'shall stop her mouth' and the other versions render the perfect 'qāfeṣāh' as a future. The verb 'weyitboneNU' is plural while 'yishmor' is singular, so the verse moves from one wise man to many. The packet's commentators do not agree on how to read it: Meiri gives a second reading in which the pious themselves consider. I stayed with the plain reading and brought out the shift to the plural in the commentary.

STEPBible glosses tit'attaf as past ('was fainting'); the imperfect here is durative, so I glossed it 'keeps wrapping itself / faints'. Nefesh is rendered 'life' in the literal layer; 'soul' of the KJV would be misleading, and v.9 shows the nefesh as the throat that longs.

The verbs of vv.6-7 are wayyiqtol 'cried' followed by yiqtol 'delivers' (ya-tzilem); the refrain is a narrative recounting, so I render the yiqtol as a habitual present 'he would deliver'. KJV and ASV use the simple past, YLT the present. I left the tense of the refrain ambiguous in the literal layer.

STEPBible glosses nefesh as 'a throat' here; I kept 'throat' in the gloss because shokeqah ('longing, rushing') is a physical image, and used 'soul' in the dramatic layer. Radak and Meiri derive shoqeqah from the root shuq, a hollow-verb form with a doubled final consonant; their reasoning is cited in the note. Metzudat Zion's parallel is Isaiah 29:8.

Нефеш передан как «душа» только в связи с жаждой и голодом в драматическом слое — там «жизнь»; в буквальном слое «душа их», потому что по-русски «горло» исказило бы идиому, а комментарий объясняет значение слова.
Игра на корне цар/мецуким («в тесноте» — «из теснин») сохранена словами «тесно» / «теснины»; в Синодальном «скорбь» и «беды», где образ тесноты теряется.
